header:
Meeting: Hosted Embeddings + Reranker demo for Highline Media
Date: 2025-05-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Jose Ramirez (Redwood SE); Samir Gupta (Highline Head of Search); Dana Lee (Highline ML); Omar Khalid (Highline Product)
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Highline through the hosted embeddings endpoint and the reranking flow. Focus: improving search relevance for mix of short queries and long-form articles. Discussed vectordb options, end-to-end latency/cost tradeoffs, Redwood Console demo for routes and Optimize recommendations. Customer requested trial and pricing and agreed to share logs for benchmark run.
topics: Intro & goals; Current infra (Elastic + homegrown vectors); Embeddings model selection; Reranker architecture (client-side kNN then Redwood rerank); Console walkthrough (routes, metrics); Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization); Next steps & pricing
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Jose from SE will jump into the technical walk through. Samir, Dana — nice to meet you.
[00:07] Samir Gupta: Thanks Maya, yeah excited. We've sent over a quick agenda — we want to see embeddings + a rerank flow, mainly hosted, to avoid infra lift initially.
[00:15] Jose Ramirez: Cool, I'll start with high level, then live demo. Quick clarifier: when you say "rerank" are you thinking full neural re-rank after candidate recall or inline scoring?
[00:23] Dana Lee: Full re-rank after a candidate recall — we do Elasticsearch top-200 and then a model does post-retrieval scoring. We're exploring vector-first approaches too.
[00:31] Jose Ramirez: Got it. So our common pattern with hosted is: call our embeddings endpoint to index vectors (or use batch import), store vectors in your vector DB or Redwood's hosted vector store, then on query do a kNN recall and call Redwood's reranker endpoint which takes the query, top-k candidates, and returns a final ranked list with confidence scores.
[00:47] Omar Khalid: Quick Q — how does this interact with our current Elastic cluster? We want to avoid ripping everything out.
[00:54] Maya Patel: Totally reasonable. Many customers hybridize — Elastic for keyword infra, embed-and-rerank for relevance. You can do keyword + vector hybrid recall client side then call Redwood reranker, or use our prefix caching to reduce repeated token costs.
[01:10] Samir Gupta: Cost is a big one. We're worried about per-query rerank cost at peak. What do you recommend?
[01:16] Jose Ramirez: A couple levers: 1) reduce k (usually 20->50 is overkill; often 5-10 is enough after a quick validation), 2) use a smaller reranker model — Redwood's catalog includes mid-size models optimized for rerank, 3) batch multiple queries where applicable or use asynchronous scoring if latency allows. Our Optimize tool will give suggestions based on your qps distribution.
[01:34] Dana Lee: Can the reranker access the document text or just vector IDs?
[01:37] Jose Ramirez: You send candidate doc snippets or IDs plus text — options. For privacy you can pass only an ID and we can fetch from your secured blob if integrated, but for hosted we usually ask for text snippets in call to reranker to avoid extra hops.
[01:50] [01:50] Maya Patel: We'll demo both patterns — text-inlined rerank and ID+fetch.
[01:55] Jose Ramirez: Switching to the Console — sharing screen. (screen share pauses)
[02:10] Jose Ramirez: Here's the Routes page. You can see model selection for embeddings and rerank separately. For hosted route I selected embed-text-002 (an example from our curated catalog) and for rerank we picked embed-rank-medium-v1.
[02:25] Samir Gupta: That model name looks familiar, is it open?
[02:28] Jose Ramirez: It's from our curated catalog — it's an open model variant we've benchmarked for rerank. We run perf metrics and have token cost estimates in the Console.
[02:36] [02:36] Omar Khalid: How are you estimating token counts? Our queries vary a lot — sometimes 3 words, sometimes 250 words.
[02:42] Jose Ramirez: We use historical distributions — you can upload sample logs and Optimize will give a projected cost curve. For long documents we recommend passing summaries or using prefix cache to store doc embeddings and then send smaller context to the reranker.
[02:55] Samir Gupta: Could you show a curl example for embeddings and then the rerank call?
[02:58] Jose Ramirez: Yep. (switches tab) Here's a curl to create an embedding: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"model":"embed-text-002","input":"<document text>"}' — returns vector in JSON.
[03:18] Jose Ramirez: Then client-side store to vector DB. For rerank: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{"model":"embed-rank-medium-v1","query":"how do I cancel subscription","candidates":[{"id":"123","text":"..."},{"id":"456","text":"..."}] }' — returns ranked list with scores.
[03:45] Dana Lee: Any rate limits for rerank route?
[03:48] Maya Patel: There are per-account rate limits but Dedicated customers can get higher throughput. For hosted we have burst windows and you can request quota increases.
[03:56] [03:56] Samir Gupta: What about latency? We need sub-200ms tail for the rerank at p95 ideally. Is that realistic hosted?
[04:05] Jose Ramirez: For small k (<=10) and compact reranker models, p95 under 200ms is achievable on Redwood hosted in our benchmarked cases. For longer docs it climbs. We can do an A/B with your logs.
[04:18] Omar Khalid: Whoa — you mentioned prefix caching earlier. How does that work with embeddings?
[04:22] Jose Ramirez: prefix/KV cache stores precomputed model states for repeated prefixes or doc contexts — reduces token generation cost and latency for long contexts. It's more used in generation but we use similar cache patterns for rerank when the same doc text is sent repeatedly to the model.
[04:36] [04:36] Samir Gupta: Let's talk vector DBs: we'll likely use Elastic + our in-house FAISS cluster. Does Redwood recommend storing vectors in your managed vector store or keep them ourselves?
[04:45] Jose Ramirez: Tradeoffs: managed store simplifies setup and we handle scaling, backup; your control plane use-case might prefer self-hosted FAISS for data residency or cost. Redwood supports both — API-level integration is identical. For the trial we can demo with our hosted vector store for speed.
[05:02] Dana Lee: Security — for hosted vector store, where does data live and encryption? We have PII concerns.
[05:08] Maya Patel: Hosted stores are encrypted at rest and in transit, we integrate with KMS for enterprise customers. For regulated data, Private deployment or Dedicated is recommended. We'll share the SOC2 and network diagrams after this call.
[05:22] [05:22] Jose Ramirez: Demo time: I'll run a sample end-to-end. First, upload 3 sample docs, create embeddings, store in hosted vectors. (typing)
[05:36] [05:36] Jose Ramirez: Running a query now — I'll call the recall endpoint to get top 10, then call rerank. Here's the raw timings — recall 45ms, rerank 120ms, total ~165ms.
[05:49] Samir Gupta: That looks promising. What's the CPU/GPU behind rerank?
[05:53] Jose Ramirez: We run rerank on GPU-backed hosts; smaller models can run on CPU but GPU gives better tail latency. In hosted we colocate optimized kernels; for Dedicated you can choose instance types.
[06:07] [06:07] Omar Khalid: If we keep our own vectors in FAISS, will rerank pull the text over network for each call? That could add latency.
transcript_continued:
[06:14] Jose Ramirez: You can either send text snippets in the request (single hop) or provide IDs. If IDs, you can use a signed fetch endpoint so we can retrieve snippets securely; that adds network time but often negligible if the fetch is fast. For ultra-low latency we recommend inlining snippets for the top 5 candidates only.
[06:36] Samir Gupta: Any thoughts on model selection for multilingual content? We have a lot of Spanish and Portuguese content.
[06:41] Jose Ramirez: Our catalog includes multilingual embedding models. For rerank, we recommend a bilingual reranker or using language-specific rerank models. Optimize can profile language mixes and suggest model selection.
[06:55] Dana Lee: Are there any pitfalls you commonly see when people switch from exact-match-first to embed-rerank?
[07:00] Jose Ramirez: Yes — common ones: 1) over-indexing (very large k), 2) sending full doc bodies which spikes token cost, 3) not having good labeled queries to tune reranker thresholds. We recommend a small labeled validation set for precision/recall metrics before full rollout.
[07:18] Maya Patel: Speaking of validation, we have an eval harness in Redwood Optimize — you can upload a set of queries and relevance labels and it will run models and produce NDCG/MRR and cost tradeoff charts.
[07:30] Samir Gupta: Can you show the Optimize page?
[07:33] Jose Ramirez: Yep — switching to Optimize. (screen) Here you can upload a CSV, choose baseline and candidate models, and it will output performance vs cost scatter plots. You can also see suggested quantization profiles if you move to Dedicated.
[07:50] Omar Khalid: For the trial, what do you need from us to get a representative bench?
[07:54] Jose Ramirez: Sample query logs (sanitized), average doc length, and either sample stored vectors or a sample dump. From that we can simulate recall distributions and pick k.
[08:04] Dana Lee: Sanity check — does the rerank endpoint return logits or calibrated scores? We want calibrated probabilities for the UI.
[08:09] Jose Ramirez: It returns scores and confidence calibrated by default for our rerank models; you can also request raw logits. The API will label them as score/confidence in the response.
[08:20] [08:20] Samir Gupta: Example response shape?
[08:23] Jose Ramirez: Example: {"results":[{"id":"123","score":0.92,"rank":1},{"id":"456","score":0.78,"rank":2}]} — plus optional span highlights if you enable structured output.
[08:40] Omar Khalid: Are there out-of-the-box reranker explainability tools? Our PMs want to show users why results moved up.
[08:45] Jose Ramirez: We have a lightweight explainability output that returns top contributing tokens or phrases per candidate. It's heuristic and depends on the model; for deeper explainability we recommend a small model with structured output.
[08:58] Dana Lee: OK great. Can you show the Console route logs for a sample query?
[09:02] Jose Ramirez: (navigates) Here's an example trace: token-level cost, latency breakdown (recall vs rerank), and model version used. You can export traces as CSV.
[09:17] [09:17] Samir Gupta: One more question on fallback — if the rerank route errors, do you have automatic fallback to keyword-only or a smaller model?
[09:25] Maya Patel: Yes, our rollout policies support canary and fallback to a configured alternate model or to a simple keyword-backend. We can set automatic thresholds that fallback if latency or error rate passes a threshold.
[09:36] Jose Ramirez: That helps keep the UX consistent.
[09:39] Omar Khalid: Pricing again — what's the factor between embed call + rerank vs just keyword? We need a ballpark for our finance team.
transcript_final:
[09:45] Maya Patel: I'll send a cost estimate after you share logs. Quick rough: embedding is per-embedding unit and rerank is per-token processed — ballpark varies 3-7x over keyword depending on model choice and k. We'll put concrete numbers in the email.
[09:59] Samir Gupta: Sounds fair.
[10:02] Jose Ramirez: Final recap: we'll provision a short hosted trial with a couple of routes — embeddings + rerank; we'll run bench with your sample logs; Maya will send pricing and SOC2 docs; Samir will share logs.
[10:14] Maya Patel: Thanks all, I'll jot down the next steps. Any final quick Qs?
[10:19] Dana Lee: No, that's it for now. Thanks.
[10:22] Omar Khalid: Thanks everyone.
[10:25] Jose Ramirez: Thanks — we'll follow up with the trial link. End call.

Notes: transcription has some errors — model names sometimes abbreviated; timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts: https://redwood.ai/decks/highline-embed-rerank-demo.pdf; benchmark sheet (internal): https://redwood.ai/sheets/bench-highline-0509.xlsx
conclusion: Customer interested in a hosted trial. Key blockers: need cost estimate and sample logs. Recommended immediate plan: 2-week hosted trial with top-5 rerank, optimize to pick model, run bench vs Pinecone + Elastic hybrid. Set internal follow-up to confirm trial provisioning and security docs.
